title: Silithus
body: Silithus is a wasteland of sand, wind and stone in the far southwest of Kalimdor, reached on foot only by the northwestern ridge out of Un'Goro Crater. Nearly a thousand years ago the qiraji poured out of their fortress city of Ahn'Qiraj and swept across this desert in the War of the Shifting Sands. The night elves under Fandral Staghelm fought them here and lost Southwind Village, until at last the insects were sealed behind the Scarab Wall in the south. Today the silithid hives of Ashi, Zora and Regal swarm across the sands once more. The Cenarion Circle keeps watch over the wastes from Cenarion Hold at the heart of the desert and from the graves of Valor's Rest in the north. Other powers stir as well. Twilight's Hammer cultists camp across the desert, and dwarven explorers keep a camp in the southern hills.

title: Valor's Rest
body: In the far northeast of Silithus, close to the ridge that climbs out of Un'Goro Crater, lies Valor's Rest, a graveyard the Cenarion Circle calls the final resting place of those who fell in these wastes. A few of the Circle's agents keep a quiet camp beside the graves. Their leader, Layo Starstrike, receives those sent by Rabine Saturna of Nighthaven, and he warns every visitor that the past lives on in this desert and must be handled carefully, lest it wake. The tauren Jarund Stoutstrider shares his watch, and Zannok Hidepiercer sells leatherworking supplies to travelers passing through.

title: Staghelm Point
body: On a high peak in northeastern Silithus stands Staghelm Point, an old night elven tower looking out over the desert. Its lone keeper is Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher, a night elf who says it was here, nearly a thousand years ago, that the qiraji began their march of destruction across Kalimdor. She has been slain a hundred times and always wakes again at her post. Some call her cursed, others a herald of a new age, and she herself warns that ancient forces stir and that nightmares now come out of the Dream. A bronze drake of the Brood of Nozdormu circles in the sky nearby, and cultists of the Twilight's Hammer camp close by.

title: Twilight's Run
body: Twilight's Run is a cave tucked into the northeast corner of Silithus, one of the Twilight's Hammer's bases of operation in the desert. Outside its mouth the cult keeps a camp of overlords, masters and flamereavers, and within the tunnels dwells Vyral the Vile, the local leader of the cult in Silithus, who carries a signet ring. The druids of Cenarion Hold count the horrors of the cave as formidable indeed, and Huum Wildmane names Vyral among the heads of the serpent that the Circle means to strike.

title: Hive'Ashi
body: North of Cenarion Hold the sand rises into the mounds of Hive'Ashi, the northern of the three great silithid hives of Silithus. Swarmers, stingers, defenders and sandstalkers boil across its slopes while workers labor below, and the truesilver veins there come coated in ooze. A rare and dangerous silithid called Rex Ashil is sometimes seen among them. Inside, as in each of its sister hives, stands a crystal carved with qiraji glyphs, and the dwarves of the Bronzebeard camp suspect these crystals are tied to the swarms now pouring from the hives. A Cenarion scout, Jalia, lies hidden nearby to watch, certain that greater, darker powers drive the insects.

title: Cenarion Hold
body: Cenarion Hold is the fortress of the Cenarion Circle at the heart of Silithus, raised where an old night elven settlement stood, to guard against what lies sealed in the south. The infantry of the hold deal harshly with anyone who spills blood on neutral ground, Captain Vish Kozus keeps watch from the top of the watchtower, and flight masters link the hold to the rest of Kalimdor. At the inn, Calandrath misses the birds and trees of Auberdine and wonders how anyone makes the bitter sandworm meat of the desert fit to eat. A bronze drake circles overhead.

title: Twilight Base Camp and Twilight Post
body: West of Cenarion Hold the Twilight's Hammer has pitched two of its camps, Twilight Base Camp and, farther west, Twilight Post. Geolords, avengers and stonecallers of the cult crowd their tents and perform rituals day and night, and the druids suspect those rituals are linked to the pulsing red crystals scattered across the desert. In each camp stand wind stones, lesser, common and greater, through which the cultists summon powerful elemental nobles and take their orders. Twilight Keepers such as Havunth and Mayna guard chapters of the cult's secret lexicon, and prophets travel between the camps under heavy escort. The cult's cooks hunt sandworms for food, though how they make the bitter meat palatable is anyone's guess.

title: The Crystal Vale
body: In the far northwest corner of Silithus lies the Crystal Vale, a valley rich in thorium and ruled by elementals of earth and air. Desert rumblers lumber across its floor, dust stormers whirl across it, and a fierce elemental named Huricanian is said to roam there. Duke Hydraxis of the Waterlords counts the vale's stormers and rumblers among the foes he would see destroyed. Within the vale lie the remains of the Ravaged Twilight Camp. The cult once thrived there, but now scattered wood, canvas and fragments of clay tablet are all that mark the spot. A lone human, Highlord Demitrian, keeps vigil over the ruin and bids visitors look upon it and know the power the elements hold.

title: Southwind Village
body: In eastern Silithus lie the ruins of Southwind Village, once the night elves' base of operations in this land. It fell in the War of the Shifting Sands and was overrun by the silithid, who have held it ever since. The tortured spirits of fallen druids and sentinels still wander the broken streets, led by the Shade of Ambermoon, and their death wails rouse the hive that has claimed the village tower, around which a mass of wasps endlessly circles. The druids of Nighthaven believe a Reliquary of Purity was left here long ago.

title: Bones of Grakkarond
body: South of Cenarion Hold lie the Bones of Grakkarond, the remains of a great dragon stretched across the open desert. Dredge crushers and stonelash scorpids prowl among them, cyclone warriors whirl past, and desert rumblers lumber through the sand. Who the dragon was in life, and how it came to die here, the desert does not say. To most who pass it seems a forgotten place, one more field of bones in a land that has seen too many.

parts.body: It matters to the qiraji after all. A hive crystal's glyphs picture their emissary meeting three silithid at a great dragon's bones, and Geologist Larksbane is sure these are the bones in question. A code of calling traced in the sand here, she reasons, would bring the overlords first and then the emissary, each believing fresh messages wait to be carried.

She was right. Her glyphs, traced in the sand among the bones, called down the silithid overlords and at last the emissary itself, and when it fell, the means to unlock the crystal's hidden messages was taken from its body.

title: Hive'Zora
body: Hive'Zora sprawls across western Silithus, its mounds crawling with wasps. Hive sisters, reavers, waywatchers and tunnelers guard the hive, and a rare silithid called Zora lurks within. Deep in a tunnel full of the insects hides Cenarion Scout Azenel, who would much rather be elsewhere but means to watch the silithid day in and day out for as long as it takes to help win the war. Silithyst geysers break through the dunes around the hive.

title: Hive'Regal
body: Hive'Regal is the southern hive of Silithus, the haunt of slavemakers, spitfires, ambushers, burrowers and hive lords, with a rare beast called Lapress among them. Stonelash flayers and rock stalkers hunt the sands around its mounds. Like its sister hives it guards a crystal carved with qiraji glyphs. Deep in its tunnels Cenarion Scout Landion creeps close enough to the insects to go unnoticed, though he would not advise anyone to try it.

title: Bronzebeard Encampment
body: In the southern hills of Silithus, east of the Scarab Wall, the dwarves of Brann Bronzebeard's expedition have made camp. They came to search the hives for lost artifacts, and between the four of them, monkey included, they speak thirty-eight languages, Titan among them. Brann himself has gone missing again. Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge stay on with Brann's monkey Glibb, sure they are onto something huge, though their pleas to Ironforge for an army go unanswered. In the mountains behind the camp hunts Deathclasp, a giant scorpid.

title: Twilight Outpost
body: Far in the southwest of Silithus, not far from the Scarab Wall, stands Twilight Outpost, the southernmost of the Twilight's Hammer camps. Geolords, avengers and stonecallers fill it, with Twilight Masters among them, and a prophet passes through under heavy escort. Twilight Keeper Exeter guards a chapter of the cult's lexicon nearby. Wind stones of every size, lesser, common and greater, stand among the tents for the cult to call on the elemental powers it serves, and at times a Twilight Lord named Everun is seen walking the camp.

title: The Scarab Wall
body: In the far southwest of Silithus runs the Scarab Wall, raised at the end of the War of the Shifting Sands to seal the qiraji and their silithid within Ahn'Qiraj. For a thousand years it has stood. Near this sacred barrier lies a single crystalline tear, left as a symbol of the great losses of that war. Scorpids creep along the foot of the wall, and a rare creature called Setis is known to prowl there.

When the War of the Shifting Sands ended they were sealed with the insects behind them, and for a thousand years nothing passed through. Before them rises the Scarab Dais, a broad stone platform at the foot of the wall. Beyond the gates lie the ruins of the outer city and, deeper within, the temple of the qiraji.

title: Commander Mar'alith
body: Commander Mar'alith leads the Cenarion Circle's forces at Cenarion Hold, a night elf warrior bound by duty to his outpost even while his heart is elsewhere. His beloved Natalia has gone missing after weeks of strange behavior, talking to herself when she thought no one was near and insisting that her research must go on, and the captain of his guard admits he has not been himself since. Those who come to him find him distracted, asking why this has come now, with so much work still to be done. Still the war is his to run, and he rewards well those who bring him word of the Twilight's Hammer.

title: Baristolth of the Shifting Sands
body: Baristolth of the Shifting Sands is a night elf who lingers among the tents of Cenarion Hold with his eyes on the desert. A thousand years ago, he says, death had all but claimed him when a great one of the bronze dragonflight breathed once upon his broken body and let the sands of time heal his wounds, then bound him to remain a Watcher for as long as he must. Now the land shudders, the hive stirs and the drakes of the Brood of Nozdormu have returned to the skies, and Baristolth knows a second war is upon them. The time has come to keep a promise he made in that long-ago war.

In time he owned that he had kept much in secret, for enemies abound, he said, even under their very noses. With an apology he handed over an old tome on the war he had lived through, and sent his chosen on to seek his master.

title: Geologist Larksbane
body: Geologist Larksbane is a dwarf scholar serving the Cenarion Circle at Cenarion Hold, and she hears what others miss: a humming from the crystals of the desert that grows louder every day, which she believes is driving the silithid mad. Her work turns on the hidden writings of Silithus. She gathers the clay tablets left in a ruined Twilight's Hammer camp in the northwest to learn what the cult is doing here, and she studies the glyphed crystals that the qiraji have set within the hives.

title: Huum and Bor Wildmane
body: The tauren brothers Huum and Bor Wildmane are druids of the Cenarion Circle at Cenarion Hold who keep watch on an enemy most others overlook. While every eye is on the silithid, they track the Twilight's Hammer. Huum, the elder, hears the spirits of Silithus weeping for the woeful tale the land has to tell, and he directs the strikes against the cult's geolords and its local leader. Bor is blunter. He gathers up the cult's coded papers just to keep them out of circulation, and he wants the elemental templars the cultists summon given a proper beating, since nothing throws troops into disarray like taking out the chain of command.

parts.body: In time Huum learned that the cult answers to something darker still: the Abyssal Council, master of the Hammer by way of its wind stones. The brothers' war on the cult became a war on the Council, and Huum sent the Circle's heroes to Aurel Goldleaf, whose craft the next gambit would need.

Bor sends only true armies against a lord of the Council, and he admits he would do anything to leave his post and wrestle one of those things himself. When one was brought down at last he could hardly believe it, and handed over the biggest chest in the hold, filled with the best of what they had found.

title: Hermit Ortell
body: Hermit Ortell is a human who, rumor has it, once belonged to the Twilight's Hammer and deserted his sect. He hides in a cave in the mountains south of Southwind Village and lives there as a hermit, wanting nothing to do with strangers, and he sends off anyone who comes calling. Those who do find him are met with suspicion and a string of questions: how did they find him, who are they, and were they followed?

parts.body: Yet an enemy of the cult is a friend of his. The Twilight's Hammer hunts him like a beast to this day, and he knows the code its scribes use and the book that unlocks it, the Twilight Lexicon, whose three chapters the cult keeps apart.

With the Lexicon in his hands he reads the cult's secret monthly bulletin, the True Believer, watching for word that the search for him has made progress or been called off. Whatever else of use he learns from it, he is willing to pass on.

title: Highlord Demitrian
body: Highlord Demitrian, a human, keeps a strange vigil in the ruined Twilight's Hammer camp of the Crystal Vale, bidding visitors look upon the ravaged field and behold the might of the elements. He speaks of the Old Gods as the makers of the world, cast down by the Titans, and the lord he serves is Thunderaan, Prince of Air. In the Elemental Sundering, he says, Ragnaros's lieutenants Geddon and Garr betrayed Thunderaan, and the Firelord struck him down with Sulfuras and fed on his essence. What remained was sealed in a talisman of binding, broken in two and given to those lieutenants. Demitrian holds the vessel of his master's rebirth and wants elementium and the Firelord's essence to free him.

Thunderaan rose from his bonds as an enemy and had to be cut down, and his victors came back to force the lying wretch to wake the blade made from his betrayal. Demitrian only cowered before them and begged to be left to reshape his pathetic life.

title: Windcaller Proudhorn
body: Windcaller Proudhorn, a tauren of the Cenarion Circle, welcomes the volunteers who answer the call raised by the Circle's emissaries in Orgrimmar and Ironforge. The silithid, those emissaries warn, have been left unchecked too long and are preparing to spread, and tremors near hives all across Azeroth betray their swelling numbers. Proudhorn is sure that while Cenarion Hold stands, victory over the silithid is certain, provided the supplies keep coming. To her mind the desert worms threaten the caravans more than the insects do: dredge strikers recently ravaged a whole shipment of morrowgrain, and their larger southern cousins wait to move in.
sources: creature 15187 Jademoon in Ironforge, 15188 Blackhoof in Orgrimmar

title: The Twilight Mystery
body: Geologist Larksbane of Cenarion Hold wants to know what the Twilight's Hammer is doing in Silithus. A camp of the cult once thrived northwest of the hold, but anyone who goes there now finds the ground swarming with elementals and only scattered wood and canvas to mark where the tents stood. From the site she has recovered a few fragments of a clay tablet, too few to piece together anything useful, and she needs someone to brave the elementals and gather the rest so the tablet can be restored and read.
notes: Check: the diary moved off DONE 8279: the transcription (item 20405) is 8287's StartItem, handed over on accepting 8287, so part 3 (DONE 8279) keeps Ortell's decoding, new part 4 (ACCEPT 8287) the diary and the hand-off with Ortell's hope (8287 description), part 5 (DONE 8287) Mar'alith's verdict. The opening keeps Larksbane's request (8284 description). Larksbane is state 3 under mod-individual-progression, like 8284. parts.body: Restored, the tablet held words she could read but no meaning, for the cult's sects are known to hide their writings in code. It needed someone who knew more of such things, and rumor told of a cultist named Ortell who had deserted his sect and lived as a hermit in the mountains south of Southwind Village.

Found, Ortell was suspicious, then eager, since anyone who fought the cult was a friend of his. To break the code he needed the Twilight Lexicon, the book the cult's scribes use, whose three chapters it keeps apart in the hands of its Twilight Keepers at different camps.
sources: creature_loot_template: Lexicon chapters from Twilight Keepers Mayna, Exeter, Havunth

parts.body: With all three chapters gathered he set to work at once, swapping every third word with one from the second chapter and every other word with one from the first, then stopping to wonder aloud whether he had it backwards.

What came out, he declared, was a valuable chunk of information: a cultist's diary of pilgrims come to Silithus to raise a wind stone through which to commune with their masters. Having watched the Circle's forces arrive to drive the cult out, he sent the decoded parchment to Commander Mar'alith, hoping it would soon put him beyond the cult's grasp for good.
sources: item 20405 Decoded Tablet Transcription (8287 StartItem), page_text 2807-2809

parts.body: Commander Mar'alith found the parchment very interesting indeed. It shed new light on the cult's presence in Silithus, he said, and would surely help the Circle in its struggle against the Twilight's Hammer, and he rewarded its bearer handsomely.

title: Dearest Natalia
body: Commander Mar'alith's beloved Natalia has vanished. For weeks before, she had been acting strangely, talking to herself when no one was around and insisting that all was well and that her research must be allowed to go on. She was last seen heading for the dwarven camp of Bronzebeard's expedition in the south. The commander's soldiers are spread too thin to search, and duty binds him to his post, so he asks for help: go to the dwarves and question them about what became of her.

parts.body: Rutgar Glyphshaper told how she had been the first from the hold to join their forays into the hives, until in Hive'Regal she pressed her cheek to a glyphed crystal and fell into a trance. The druids woke her, but weeks later she came back demanding they return. Frankal Stonebridge told the rest: she chanted to someone who was not there, then attacked, eyes aglow, flaying their minds, until Glibb drove her off and she fled into the hive. Mar'alith resolved that, alive or dead, she must be found.

Deep in Hive'Regal waited the one she had become, Natalia Mar'alith, High Priestess of C'Thun, crying that C'Thun would retake this world. When word of it reached him, the grieving commander clutched at his chest and could only ask what C'Thun was.
sources: creature_template 15215 subname High Priestess of C'Thun; creature_text 15215

title: The Prophecy of C'Thun
body: Since Natalia Mar'alith's madness the three hives of Silithus have been spewing out bugs, and the dwarves of the Bronzebeard camp want to know why. Rutgar Glyphshaper suspects the glyphs covering the strange crystals inside the hives, and he wants rubbings taken from the crystals of Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora and Hive'Regal so the dwarves can make sense of the madness. Frankal Stonebridge has his own plan: an elixir to help read the tongue of the silithid and the qiraji, for which he needs a brain from the silithid of each hive.
notes: Converted: the chain moved out of the opening: the prism (ACCEPT 8314), Larksbane's reading of it (ACCEPT 8315), the calling (DONE 8315), her warning (DONE of Armaments of War, 8316 and class versions 8376-8382, autocomplete). The opening keeps the dwarves' requests (8309, 8310). What the prophecy says is not told: it rests only on creature_text 15183, which is never said in this core. Earlier: verified against 8309, 8310, 8314, 8315, 8316. 8309 and 8310 (QuestType 2, exclusive group -8309, both after 8304) are the entry points. No Valstann or prophecy retelling. Faction 0.

parts.body: From the rubbings the dwarves recreated the glyphs on a crystal prism, a means, they found, for the qiraji and other unknown powers to send messages to the silithid. That was all they could learn. The prism would not give up its messages, so they sent it to Geologist Larksbane at Cenarion Hold.

Larksbane saw why. There was nothing to decipher until the prism's shifting outer layer aligned with the markings within. Its one clue showed an emissary of the qiraji meeting three silithid at the bones of a large dragon, and above it a code she copied as glyphs of calling for the Bones of Grakkarond.

Drawn in the sand at the bones, the glyphs brought the overlords and then the emissary, and from the emissary came the key to the crystal. Larksbane exclaimed that she held twenty thousand years of history in her hands.
What that history foretold shook her. Should the prophecy ever come to pass, she warned, the future of them all could be at an end, and war, with untold horrors, was coming to the desert.
sources: quests 8316, 8376-8382 reward text (Armaments of War, autocomplete)

title: The Abyssal Council
body: The Twilight's Hammer has set up camps across Silithus and performs rituals in them day and night. The druids of Cenarion Hold do not yet know its plans, though they suspect a link with the pulsing red crystals spread across the desert, and Huum Wildmane means to strike first at the heads of the serpent, the Twilight geolords, and then at the cult's local leader. His brother Bor has watched cultists call up mighty elemental nobles and receive orders from them. Whether these are the beings the cult worships or messengers of something greater, none can say.

parts.body: The geolords fell, and then Vyral the Vile, slain in the cave of Twilight's Run, his signet ring carried back to Huum. The druid hailed it as doom for the cult's operations in Silithus, a blow from which it would not easily recover, though some of them still scurried about.

Any hope that the cult's work in Silithus was slowing proved mistaken. Through the arcane wind stones dotted among its camps, the Hammer answers to an even darker power, the Abyssal Council, and the night elf craftswoman Aurel Goldleaf has devised a gambit to strike at it.

parts.body: A replica of the cult's medallion of station, made with a brilliant shard and the crests of slain templars, lets a hero in twilight trappings commune through a wind stone as a mid-ranking cultist and lure a duke of the Council into ambush. Bor rewards every signet brought back.

A ring of lordship, worn by the cult's highest ranks, fools even the lords of the Council through the greater wind stones. Bor warned that such a foe calls for a true army. The lords meet the impostors with fury, swearing that this world will fall to darkness, but one was brought down, and Bor could hardly believe it.

title: The Spirits of Southwind
body: Layo Starstrike of Valor's Rest believes the Cenarion Circle's work in Silithus should begin at the ruins of Southwind Village to the southwest, once a night elf base of operations and long since overrun by the hives. He was not alive for the great tribulations of the old war, but he hopes the Circle can bring an end to a threat that was supposed to have died generations ago. First, the tortured spirits of druids and sentinels who wander the ruins must be freed, for no being, Alliance or Horde, deserves to be trapped as a tortured spirit.

parts.body: Freeing them proved Layo's suspicion that the great hive near the village had played a part in its ruin, for each death wail roused the insects, the silithid being keenly sensitive to their surroundings. He asked that the hive be stirred on purpose, from the top of the village tower where the wasps swarm thickest.

What came out of the hive was a box-shaped thing so encrusted in chitin it could barely be recognized, though one exposed corner hinted at a book beneath. If it was a journal or a log from ancient times, preserved in its shell, it might give the Circle a window into the past.

Layo sent it to Umber, the Circle's archivist in Nighthaven, touched, he admits, but brilliant, a man who has saved tomes in far worse shape. If it could be saved, Umber would do it. What he found is a tale for Moonglade.

title: The Scepter of the Shifting Sands
body: Baristolth of the Shifting Sands has waited a thousand years for a sign, and now the hive stirs once more around Cenarion Hold. In the old war, he says, the bronze flight bound him to remain as a Watcher, and he made a promise then that he means to keep. Before he can act he must be sure of one thing. War has come again, he believes, and so he asks a seeker to venture to the Caverns of Time in Tanaris and learn whether his master of the bronze has returned.

parts.body: The master had risen. Baristolth's watch was ended, and the trials began: only one could rise from the throng of would-be champions to become an ally of the Brood, and the first proof was the head of Broodlord Lashlayer from the lair of the Lord of Blackrock.

The Brood of Nozdormu distrusts the lesser races, a distrust rooted, Baristolth hinted, in much history best told by the Brood itself. To prove the champion to his master he demanded silithid carapace from the three hives by the hundred, and granted the right to deputize helpers.
sources: quest 8301 description, request and reward text

parts.body: His tome, The War of the Shifting Sands, began with Fandral Staghelm and his son. Valstann was ordered to defend Southwind Village and died when it fell. Fandral pushed on in grief, but the qiraji overran Silithus and drove the night elves back to Tanaris, where a humbled Staghelm pleaded with Anachronos. The dragon refused to involve the bronze flight until the qiraji attacked the Caverns of Time.
sources: item 20415 The War of the Shifting Sands (8303 StartItem), page_text 2793-2799

parts.body: Even the bronze flight could not stem the tide, so Anachronos called on Merithra of the green, Caelestrasz of the red and Arygos of the blue. Above Ahn'Qiraj they sensed a hidden power shielding its temple, and resolved to raise a barrier from the essence of night elves and dragons, making the city its own prison.

Anachronos sent the champion back to Silithus, to a crystalline tear beside the Scarab Wall that stands for the losses of that war. Its sorrow nearly overwhelms those who gaze into it, and within its depths a long forgotten memory stirs.

The memory showed the sealing. Anachronos halted the sands of time and conjured glyphs of warding while Staghelm called forth the roots, and the barrier closed. Then Anachronos offered Staghelm the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, the key that could open it at the gong. Staghelm refused another burden, swore he would have his son back, and hurled the scepter into the barrier, shattering it.
sources: creature_text 15381, 15382 (vision event of 8519: Anachronos the Ancient, Fandral Staghelm)

parts.body: After Staghelm's betrayal Anachronos gathered the pieces and divided them among the flights of the four mighty Aspects, thinking a scepter so divided could never be restored by those seeking chaos. He calls himself a fool for it, for even now that cursed flight hunts him.

The guardians of the shards were Eranikus, Vaelastrasz and Azuregos, watchers of the world, and each had fallen to tragedy, through agents of the Old Gods or betrayal by friends, his own naivety partly to blame. It is this, Anachronos admits, that fuels his distrust of mortals.

parts.body: Anachronos greeted the champion as one long foretold. A thousand years had passed, he said, and just as fated, one now stood before him who would lead their people into a new age. The Old God trembles, he warned, for it fears that faith and knows the might of Kalimdor comes with the champion. Shatter the prophecy of C'Thun, he urged, and when the champion was ready he would grant the Scepter of the Shifting Sands.

parts.body: The champion struck the Scarab Gong, and the ancient gates of Ahn'Qiraj opened, revealing the horrors of a forgotten war. From the ground beside the gong sprang a crystal, a token, perhaps, of the Brood's favor.
